$comment: First-load JavaScript per route, in kilobytes: the size on disk of every
chunk the production build's manifests say a route loads to render —
the runtime in build-manifest.json's rootMainFiles, the route's
entryJSFiles in its client reference manifest, and whatever its
react-loadable-manifest.json lists. Uncompressed: what ships over the wire
is smaller, but this is the number that tracks what was added.
Keys are app routes as path patterns: /decision-flows/[id], not a URL.
Every route in the build is measured; a route with no budget here is held
to the default. A budget naming a route the build does not have fails.
What it does not see: code a route loads at runtime that none of those
manifests names — a bare import() in a client component, a chunk fetched
for a client component that arrives only in a later RSC payload. See
tests/bundle/route-chunks.ts; measure in a browser with
scripts/measure-route-payload.mjs when that is the question.
Reset on 2026-09-19, when the check moved from a browser to the manifests:
the manifest measurement plus 10%, rounded up to 10 kB. It had been 15%,
covering run-to-run noise as well as growth; one build now gives one
number, so the margin is for growth alone. The two methods agreed on every
budgeted route to a tenth of a kilobyte. /creatives rose 780 → 800 by the
rule, not because it grew: its old budget left it 8% of headroom. The
default stays at 820; the heaviest route held to it is
/targeting-policies, at 764.9.
The descriptor registry (40 kB) and the panel registry with the list-detail
host (54 kB) still load whole on every route that touches either — that is
most of what /offers, /creatives and /settings carry above the shell
(G-111). When W-080 splits them, lower these to match.
Raising a budget is a decision, not a formality: say in the commit message
what got bigger and why it earns its place.
